sources.title: Notice of Termination of 14 Discretionary Federal Advisory Committees

status_summary: A Federal Register notice dated 2025-06-04 and published 2025-06-10 states that the Secretary terminated 14 discretionary advisory committees effective 2025-02-28 under Executive Order 14217, finding their purposes fulfilled: two at BEA, three at the Census Bureau, five at ITA and four at NOAA. The Commerce advisory committee page (updated 2026-07-14) says three presidential advisory committees and one discretionary committee were not renewed and ended on 2025-09-30, labels 20 committees as terminated or lapsed, and lists 45 still active without marking which are statutory. Neither source describes a department-wide review of statutory status or any reconstitution of the remaining committees' membership.

timeline.event: Effective date of the Secretary's termination of 14 discretionary Commerce advisory committees at BEA, the Census Bureau, ITA and NOAA, announced in a Federal Register notice dated 2025-06-04 and published 2025-06-10.

Three presidential advisory committees and one discretionary Commerce committee are not renewed and terminate, per the Commerce advisory committee page (committees not named in the narrative; the table marks the President's Export Council, its export administration subcommittee, the Doing Business in Africa council and NTIA's spectrum advisory committee as terminated).

title: Review Commerce advisory committees, abolish non-statutory ones, reconstitute the rest
uncertainties: The termination notice (90 FR 24383, Doc. 2025-10398, Docket DOC-2025-0010) was read by the researcher and the Commerce advisory committee page was reread in review on 2026-10-18. The notice was signed by a departmental open-government official and states the Secretary's finding. The Commerce page states a committee count of 51 while its tables list 45 committees without a terminated or lapsed marker, and its narrative accounts for 18 terminations while the tables label 20 (two are lapsed NIST and USPTO panels), so counts are approximate. The page does not classify active committees as statutory or discretionary, so whether non-statutory committees remain was not established, and it says nothing about reconstitution or membership changes. A Federal Register API search for Commerce committee documents did not surface a department-wide review or reconstitution notice. Reconstitution may have occurred without public notice; membership rosters were not reviewed. A Government Executive report on NOAA committee terminations was seen only as a search result and is not relied on. Overlap: c21-02 tracks the Census Bureau committees, which are among those terminated.
